messages.content: What is core.async and how do I use channels?

core.async is a Clojure library for asynchronous programming using channels and go blocks. It brings CSP (Communicating Sequential Processes) to Clojure.

**Setup**
```clojure
;; deps.edn
{:deps {org.clojure/core.async {:mvn/version "1.6.681"}}}

(require '[clojure.core.async :as async
           :refer [chan go go-loop <! >! <!! >!! close! put! take!
                   alts! alts!! timeout buffer sliding-buffer
                   dropping-buffer]])
```

**Core Concepts**
- **Channel**: Queue for passing values between threads/go blocks
- **go block**: Lightweight thread (parked, not OS thread)
- **<!** and **>!**: Take and put inside go blocks (parking)
- **<!!** and **>!!**: Take and put outside go blocks (blocking)

**Basic Channels**
```clojure
;; Create channel
(def ch (chan))         ; Unbuffered channel
(def ch (chan 10))      ; Buffered channel (holds 10 items)

;; Put and take (blocking - use outside go blocks)
(>!! ch "hello")        ; Put value (blocks if full)
(<!! ch)                ; Take value (blocks if empty)
;; => "hello"

;; Close channel
(close! ch)             ; No more puts allowed
(<!! ch)                ; Takes return nil when closed and empty
```

**Go Blocks**
```clojure
;; go blocks are lightweight "threads"
;; <! and >! park (don't block real thread)

(def ch (chan))

;; Producer
(go
  (dotimes [i 5]
    (>! ch i)           ; Put i to channel (parks if full)
    (println "Put" i))
  (close! ch))

;; Consumer
(go
  (loop []
    (when-let [v (<! ch)]  ; Take from channel (parks if empty)
      (println "Got" v)
      (recur))))

;; Output (interleaved):
;; Put 0
;; Got 0
;; Put 1
;; Got 1
;; ...
```

**go-loop (Common Pattern)**
```clojure
;; go-loop = (go (loop ...))
(def ch (chan))

;; Consumer with go-loop
(go-loop []
  (when-let [msg (<! ch)]
    (println "Processing:" msg)
    (recur)))

;; Producer
(go
  (doseq [x ["a" "b" "c"]]
    (>! ch x))
  (close! ch))
```

**Buffered Channels**
```clojure
;; Regular buffer - blocks when full
(def ch (chan 3))
(>!! ch 1)  ; ok
(>!! ch 2)  ; ok
(>!! ch 3)  ; ok
(>!! ch 4)  ; blocks! buffer full

;; Sliding buffer - drops oldest when full
(def ch (chan (sliding-buffer 3)))
(>!! ch 1) (>!! ch 2) (>!! ch 3)
(>!! ch 4)  ; Doesn't block, drops 1
(<!! ch)    ; => 2 (oldest remaining)

;; Dropping buffer - drops newest when full
(def ch (chan (dropping-buffer 3)))
(>!! ch 1) (>!! ch 2) (>!! ch 3)
(>!! ch 4)  ; Doesn't block, 4 is dropped
(<!! ch)    ; => 1 (4 was never added)
```

**Timeout Channels**
```clojure
;; timeout creates a channel that closes after ms
(let [ch (chan)
      t (timeout 1000)]  ; 1 second timeout
  (go
    (let [[v c] (alts! [ch t])]  ; Wait for either
      (if (= c t)
        (println "Timeout!")
        (println "Got:" v)))))

;; Timeout pattern
(defn fetch-with-timeout [ch timeout-ms]
  (go
    (let [[v c] (alts! [ch (timeout timeout-ms)])]
      (if v
        {:success v}
        {:error :timeout}))))
```

**alts! - Waiting on Multiple Channels**
```clojure
;; alts! waits on multiple channels, returns [value channel]
(let [ch1 (chan)
      ch2 (chan)]
  (go (>! ch1 "from ch1"))
  (go (>! ch2 "from ch2"))
  
  (go
    (let [[v ch] (alts! [ch1 ch2])]
      (condp = ch
        ch1 (println "Got from ch1:" v)
        ch2 (println "Got from ch2:" v)))))

;; With timeout
(go
  (let [[v ch] (alts! [data-chan (timeout 5000)])]
    (if v
      (process v)
      (println "Timed out waiting for data"))))

;; Priority (try channels in order)
(alts! [ch1 ch2 ch3] :priority true)
```

**put! and take! (Callback-based)**
```clojure
;; put! and take! are async with callbacks
;; Good for interop with callback-based code

(def ch (chan))

;; Async put
(put! ch "hello" (fn [success?]
                    (println "Put succeeded:" success?)))

;; Async take
(take! ch (fn [val]
            (println "Got:" val)))

;; No callback
(put! ch "hello")  ; Fire and forget
```
How do I use pipelines and transducers with core.async?

core.async integrates beautifully with transducers for efficient data processing.

**Channels with Transducers**
```clojure
(require '[clojure.core.async :as async :refer [chan go <! >! <!! >!! close!]])

;; Channel with transducer
(def ch (chan 10 (map inc)))  ; Buffer of 10, increment all values

(go (>! ch 1))
(<!! ch)  ; => 2 (1 + 1)

;; Composed transducers
(def ch (chan 10 (comp
                   (filter even?)
                   (map #(* % 2))
                   (take 5))))

;; Multiple transforms
(def process-xf
  (comp
    (map parse-json)
    (filter valid?)
    (map transform)
    (remove nil?)))

(def processing-chan (chan 100 process-xf))
```

**Exception Handler**
```clojure
;; Transducers can throw - provide exception handler
(def ch (chan 10 
          (map #(/ 100 %))  ; Division by zero possible
          (fn [ex]
            (println "Error:" (.getMessage ex))
            nil)))  ; Return value for error cases

(go (>! ch 0))  ; Would throw, but handler catches
```

**pipeline**
```clojure
;; pipeline runs transducer across multiple "threads" (go blocks)
(require '[clojure.core.async :refer [pipeline pipeline-blocking pipeline-async]])

(def in-ch (chan 100))
(def out-ch (chan 100))

;; 4 parallel workers
(pipeline 4                ; Parallelism
          out-ch           ; Output channel  
          (map expensive-transform)  ; Transducer
          in-ch)           ; Input channel

;; Producer
(go
  (doseq [item items]
    (>! in-ch item))
  (close! in-ch))

;; Consumer
(go-loop []
  (when-let [result (<! out-ch)]
    (process-result result)
    (recur)))
```

**pipeline-blocking vs pipeline-async**
```clojure
;; pipeline - for pure transforms (uses go blocks)
(pipeline 4 out (map transform) in)

;; pipeline-blocking - for blocking IO (uses real threads)
(pipeline-blocking 4 out 
  (map (fn [url] (http/get url)))  ; Blocking HTTP call
  in)

;; pipeline-async - for async operations
(pipeline-async 4 out
  (fn [val result-ch]
    ;; Put result to result-ch when done
    (async-fetch val #(do (async/>!! result-ch %) 
                          (async/close! result-ch))))
  in)
```

**onto-chan and to-chan**
```clojure
;; to-chan - collection to channel
(def ch (async/to-chan! [1 2 3 4 5]))
(<!! ch)  ; => 1
(<!! ch)  ; => 2

;; onto-chan! - put collection onto existing channel
(def ch (chan))
(async/onto-chan! ch [1 2 3] true)  ; true = close after

;; onto-chan! with false - don't close
(async/onto-chan! ch [1 2 3] false)
(async/onto-chan! ch [4 5 6] true)  ; Close after second batch
```

**into-chan**
```clojure
;; Collect channel into collection
(def ch (async/to-chan! [1 2 3 4 5]))

(<!! (async/into [] ch))  ; => [1 2 3 4 5]

;; With transformation
(def ch (chan 10 (map inc)))
(async/onto-chan! ch [1 2 3])
(<!! (async/into #{} ch))  ; => #{2 3 4}
```

**reduce over Channel**
```clojure
(def ch (async/to-chan! [1 2 3 4 5]))

;; Returns channel with final result
(def result-ch (async/reduce + 0 ch))
(<!! result-ch)  ; => 15

;; transduce
(def ch (async/to-chan! [1 2 3 4 5]))
(def result-ch (async/transduce (filter even?) + 0 ch))
(<!! result-ch)  ; => 6 (2 + 4)
```

**Pub/Sub**
```clojure
(require '[clojure.core.async :refer [pub sub unsub chan go-loop <! >!!]])

;; Create publisher from channel
(def events-ch (chan))
(def publisher (pub events-ch :type))  ; Dispatch on :type key

;; Create subscribers
(def user-events (chan))
(def order-events (chan))

(sub publisher :user user-events)   ; Subscribe to :user type
(sub publisher :order order-events) ; Subscribe to :order type

;; Consumers
(go-loop []
  (when-let [event (<! user-events)]
    (println "User event:" event)
    (recur)))

(go-loop []
  (when-let [event (<! order-events)]
    (println "Order event:" event)
    (recur)))

;; Publisher sends events
(>!! events-ch {:type :user :action :login :user-id 123})
;; => "User event: {:type :user ...}"

(>!! events-ch {:type :order :action :created :order-id 456})
;; => "Order event: {:type :order ...}"
```

**Mult (Broadcast)**
```clojure
(require '[clojure.core.async :refer [mult tap untap chan]])

;; mult broadcasts to multiple channels
(def source (chan))
(def m (mult source))

;; Tap into mult
(def consumer1 (chan))
(def consumer2 (chan))
(tap m consumer1)
(tap m consumer2)

;; Now both receive
(>!! source "hello")
(<!! consumer1)  ; => "hello"
(<!! consumer2)  ; => "hello"

;; Untap to stop receiving
(untap m consumer1)
```

**Processing Pipeline Example**
```clojure
(defn process-events [input-ch]
  (let [;; Parse JSON
        parsed-ch (chan 100 (map json/parse-string))
        ;; Validate
        valid-ch (chan 100 (filter valid-event?))
        ;; Transform
        transformed-ch (chan 100 (map transform-event))
        ;; Results
        results-ch (chan 100)]
    
    ;; Wire up pipeline
    (pipeline 4 parsed-ch (map json/parse-string) input-ch)
    (pipeline 4 valid-ch (filter valid-event?) parsed-ch)
    (pipeline-blocking 4 transformed-ch (map transform-event) valid-ch)
    (pipeline-blocking 4 results-ch (map save-to-db!) transformed-ch)
    
    results-ch))
```
How do I build a worker pool or rate limiter with core.async?

core.async is great for building concurrency patterns like worker pools and rate limiters.

**Worker Pool**
```clojure
(require '[clojure.core.async :as async
           :refer [chan go go-loop <! >! >!! <!! close! thread]])

(defn worker-pool
  "Creates n workers processing items from in-ch, results to out-ch"
  [n process-fn in-ch out-ch]
  (dotimes [i n]
    (go-loop []
      (when-let [item (<! in-ch)]
        (try
          (let [result (process-fn item)]
            (when result
              (>! out-ch result)))
          (catch Exception e
            (println "Worker" i "error:" (.getMessage e))))
        (recur))))
  out-ch)

;; Usage
(def jobs (chan 100))
(def results (chan 100))

;; Start 4 workers
(worker-pool 4 expensive-computation jobs results)

;; Submit jobs
(go
  (doseq [job job-list]
    (>! jobs job))
  (close! jobs))

;; Collect results
(go-loop [all-results []]
  (if-let [result (<! results)]
    (recur (conj all-results result))
    (println "All done:" (count all-results))))
```

**Worker Pool with Blocking Operations**
```clojure
;; For IO-bound work, use thread instead of go
(defn blocking-worker-pool [n process-fn in-ch out-ch]
  (dotimes [_ n]
    (thread
      (loop []
        (when-let [item (<!! in-ch)]
          (try
            (when-let [result (process-fn item)]  ; Can block!
              (>!! out-ch result))
            (catch Exception e
              (println "Error:" (.getMessage e))))
          (recur)))))
  out-ch)

;; Good for HTTP requests, database calls, file IO
(defn fetch-url [url]
  (:body (http/get url)))  ; Blocking call

(def urls-ch (chan 100))
(def results-ch (chan 100))

(blocking-worker-pool 10 fetch-url urls-ch results-ch)
```

**Rate Limiter**
```clojure
(defn rate-limiter
  "Limits throughput to n items per interval-ms"
  [n interval-ms in-ch out-ch]
  (let [tokens (chan n)]  ; Semaphore as channel
    ;; Fill with initial tokens
    (dotimes [_ n]
      (>!! tokens :token))
    
    ;; Token replenisher
    (go-loop []
      (<! (async/timeout interval-ms))
      (dotimes [_ n]
        (async/offer! tokens :token))  ; Non-blocking put
      (recur))
    
    ;; Rate-limited forwarder
    (go-loop []
      (when-let [item (<! in-ch)]
        (<! tokens)  ; Wait for token
        (>! out-ch item)
        (recur)))))

;; Usage: 10 items per second
(def unlimited (chan 1000))
(def limited (chan 1000))
(rate-limiter 10 1000 unlimited limited)
```

**Token Bucket Rate Limiter**
```clojure
(defn token-bucket
  "Token bucket rate limiter
   rate: tokens per second
   burst: max tokens (bucket size)"
  [rate burst]
  (let [tokens (atom burst)
        interval (/ 1000.0 rate)]
    ;; Refill tokens
    (go-loop []
      (<! (async/timeout (long interval)))
      (swap! tokens #(min burst (inc %)))
      (recur))
    
    ;; Return function that acquires token
    (fn acquire! []
      (loop []
        (if (pos? @tokens)
          (do (swap! tokens dec) true)
          (do (Thread/sleep 10) (recur)))))))

;; Usage
(def limiter (token-bucket 10 20))  ; 10/sec, burst of 20

(defn rate-limited-call [f & args]
  (limiter)  ; Wait for token
  (apply f args))
```

**Bounded Parallel Processing**
```clojure
(defn bounded-pmap
  "Like pmap but with bounded parallelism using core.async"
  [n f coll]
  (let [in-ch (chan)
        out-ch (chan)]
    ;; Start workers
    (dotimes [_ n]
      (go-loop []
        (when-let [[idx item] (<! in-ch)]
          (>! out-ch [idx (f item)])
          (recur))))
    
    ;; Submit work with index
    (let [indexed (map-indexed vector coll)
          cnt (count coll)]
      (go
        (doseq [item indexed]
          (>! in-ch item))
        (close! in-ch))
      
      ;; Collect and sort by original index
      (->> (repeatedly cnt #(<!! out-ch))
           (sort-by first)
           (map second)))))

;; Usage
(bounded-pmap 4 expensive-fn items)
```

**Request Coalescing (Debounce)**
```clojure
(defn debounce
  "Only forward last value received within wait-ms"
  [in-ch wait-ms]
  (let [out-ch (chan)]
    (go-loop [last-val nil
              timer nil]
      (let [ports (if timer [in-ch timer] [in-ch])
            [v ch] (async/alts! ports)]
        (condp = ch
          timer (do
                  (when last-val
                    (>! out-ch last-val))
                  (recur nil nil))
          in-ch (if v
                  (recur v (async/timeout wait-ms))
                  (close! out-ch)))))
    out-ch))

;; Usage - debounce search input
(def search-input (chan))
(def debounced (debounce search-input 300))

(go-loop []
  (when-let [query (<! debounced)]
    (perform-search query)
    (recur)))
```

**Batch Processing**
```clojure
(defn batch
  "Collect items into batches by size or timeout"
  [in-ch batch-size timeout-ms]
  (let [out-ch (chan)]
    (go-loop [batch []
              timer (async/timeout timeout-ms)]
      (let [[v ch] (async/alts! [in-ch timer])]
        (cond
          ;; Timeout - flush batch
          (= ch timer)
          (do
            (when (seq batch)
              (>! out-ch batch))
            (recur [] (async/timeout timeout-ms)))
          
          ;; Channel closed
          (nil? v)
          (do
            (when (seq batch)
              (>! out-ch batch))
            (close! out-ch))
          
          ;; Batch full
          (= (count batch) (dec batch-size))
          (do
            (>! out-ch (conj batch v))
            (recur [] (async/timeout timeout-ms)))
          
          ;; Add to batch
          :else
          (recur (conj batch v) timer))))
    out-ch))

;; Usage - batch database inserts
(def events (chan 1000))
(def batched (batch events 100 5000))  ; 100 items or 5 seconds

(go-loop []
  (when-let [batch (<! batched)]
    (db/insert-batch! batch)  ; Efficient batch insert
    (recur)))
```

**Circuit Breaker**
```clojure
(defn circuit-breaker
  [failure-threshold reset-timeout-ms]
  (let [failures (atom 0)
        state (atom :closed)  ; :closed, :open, :half-open
        last-failure (atom 0)]
    
    (fn [f]
      (case @state
        :open
        (if (> (- (System/currentTimeMillis) @last-failure) reset-timeout-ms)
          (do (reset! state :half-open)
              (try
                (let [result (f)]
                  (reset! state :closed)
                  (reset! failures 0)
                  result)
                (catch Exception e
                  (reset! state :open)
                  (reset! last-failure (System/currentTimeMillis))
                  (throw e))))
          (throw (ex-info "Circuit open" {:state :open})))
        
        (:closed :half-open)
        (try
          (let [result (f)]
            (when (= @state :half-open)
              (reset! state :closed)
              (reset! failures 0))
            result)
          (catch Exception e
            (swap! failures inc)
            (when (>= @failures failure-threshold)
              (reset! state :open)
              (reset! last-failure (System/currentTimeMillis)))
            (throw e)))))))

;; Usage
(def breaker (circuit-breaker 5 30000))  ; 5 failures, 30s reset

(defn safe-call []
  (breaker #(risky-operation)))
```
